recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It completes the original Pharmacy WG intent with a narrow terminology-source change; related later status wording issues should remain separate.
issue_request: FHIR-13780 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for STU3 MedicationRequest. Pharmacy requested updated status definitions clarifying stopped versus cancelled: stopped should be used when some but not all administrations have occurred, and cancelled should mean no administrations have occurred.
initial_application: Historical commit eddae4c6adc0a38d7c292dfa6f82cc15e75e194e, titled 'GF #13943, GF #13879, GF #13871, GF #13780, GF #13999 - Pharmacy Resource changes', applied the issue to the old MedicationRequest spreadsheet by changing cancelled to 'withdrawn before any administrations have occurred' and stopped to 'before all of the administrations occurred'. Commit 7373e742ee4ae5907dc0d8b0779cadb0cb0892f0 migrated those definitions into the current standalone CodeSystem source.
additional_context: MedicationRequest is active in source/fhir.ini and owned by Pharmacy, so source/medicationrequest/codesystem-medicationrequest-status.xml is current build-scope terminology source. Later status wording work, especially FHIR-32859 already represented on the combined branch, changed prescription/order wording to request lifecycle wording but did not address the remaining stopped/cancelled administration boundary. Confluence and Zulip searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: Updated source/medicationrequest/codesystem-medicationrequest-status.xml so the stopped definition explicitly says actions are permanently halted after some, but before all, administrations have occurred. The existing cancelled definition already states before any administrations have occurred.
source_changes: source/medicationrequest/codesystem-medicationrequest-status.xml: clarified the stopped code definition to require some but not all administrations, preserving the existing cancelled definition for no administrations.

related_jiras.note: Later Published issue changed MedicationRequest status wording from prescription/order language to request lifecycle language and is already represented on the combined branch; it does not alter the stopped/cancelled administration distinction.
